label: Michael Della Rocca, PSR Pp.1-10: The principle of sufficient reason entails that all truths are…
locator: pp.1-10: p.1 with footnote 2 for the PSR; pp.9-10 with footnote 13 for the entailment
interpretation: Della Rocca tends to think van Inwagen and Bennett are right about this entailment, and says a clear-headed proponent of the PSR can be expected to embrace necessitarianism. 'Tend to think' is kept: the claim is his tentative agreement, and it does not state that necessitarianism is true. He is willing to go along with their assumption that no contingent proposition is a sufficient reason for itself, and his footnote's PSR gives a 'sufficient reason' on which a necessary reason would make its target necessary.
